Mr. Mayor, City Council, I'd like to provide a little bit of information regarding my background and experience and discuss how my skills could be a benefit working with the other members of the City Council. My name is Steve Kennedy, and I've been a resident of South Lyon for over 45 years. Career -wise, I've been a management consultant for almost 40 years. During that time, I've worked with many Fortune 500 companies, Helping them improve their operations, performance, and profitability. I've worked with all levels within those organizations, From the C -suite level to department head to first -line supervision and the hourly personnel. I've worked with them to help them better understand and utilize formal decision -making approaches, Approaches when addressing issues within each of their areas. This training and guidance has Helped them remove subjectivity from their decisions and help them to better separate Their wants from their needs. The subjective decision -making ability is critical when Developing, establishing, managing operating budgets, prioritizing day -to -day activities, and forecasting future needs. In addition, I've spent a number of years helping those various Companies improve their overall maintenance operations I've worked with Them to reduce operating expenses and help them to maximize asset performance In the industries in which I have worked this means fully understanding how best To spend money maintaining the equipment infrastructure and other assets owned by That firm it involves establishing a five -year asset replacement plan to Project future needs better managing spares and replacement part purchases Services, and effectively utilizing all of their maintenance resources. The resume I provided highlights the benefits that have been derived by those companies with whom I have worked. As a consultant, it's always challenging to bring about the desired changes and improvements In a company when you have absolutely no direct authority to make that happen. Success can only occur by establishing an effective rapport and collaborative working Relationship with the company's personnel so that they can implement the changes and Effectively use the provided tools and methods for long -term success since Becoming semi -retired during the past few years I've regularly attended the City Council meetings and have met and spoken with many of you during those Sessions my attendance has afforded me the opportunity to better understand the challenges facing South Lyon it has provided an opportunity for two -way Communication with the council members to obtain a more in -depth understanding Of the issues and possible solutions for them, As opposed to merely watching the videotape proceedings. So why am I applying for the City Council vacancy? I believe that my interpersonal skills and ability to work effectively with others can be beneficial in working with the other Council members and City employees To effectively address the challenges we face. Further, my background and experience with budgets, expense optimization, Utilization, maintenance, and project management, coupled with my desire to see Southline continue to evolve, can be a benefit on the Southline City Council.

On a related note, as the city's SEMCOG representative, I attended a seminar at SEMCOG's headquarters last week That dealt with the interrelationship between stormwater, wastewater, and Drinking water. One of the biggest issues facing many cities in the seven county Area in southeast Michigan deals with wastewater and the items that end up in The city drains. It was emphasized that residents should never flush personal And baby wipes, facial tissue, condoms, tampons, sanitary products, cleaning wipes, Dental floss, prescription and non -prescription drugs, cotton balls, Balls, swabs, or cigarette butts. These items can collect in the sewers and clog the pipes. In addition, all fats, oils, and greases from cooking should be disposed of in the trash And not put down the drain. When they are put down the drain, they tend to settle and Solidify and reduce the flow in our city's waste system, which can lead to backups in our residents' homes. So again, please dispose of everything properly. There are only three Three things that should be flushed down the toilet. Number one, number two, and TP. That's it. Thank you, Mr. Mayor.

This past week, Ann Arbor firefighter Amy Pennywhitt died when she was struck by a pickup truck that was driving too fast for the icy road conditions. Firefighters were responding to multiple crashes on I -94 when the pickup truck came up on them and lost control on the icy surface. The vehicle struck Pennywhitt and another firefighter as they tried to get out of the way. The other firefighter was not seriously injured while Penny Witt suffered Critical head and chest injuries. She passed away a few days later from her Injuries in the hospital. She was 34 and had been in the department for seven years. She left behind a husband, a child, other family members, and friends. While Our thoughts and prayers go out to her, to her family, and to the City of Ann Arbor Fire Department, this is an important reminder for everyone to take Weather conditions into consideration and drive appropriately move over when You see the lights flashing alongside the road and slow down help keep those safe who are working to keep you safe Thank You mr. mayor Thank You council

To begin, just a little background. The South Lyon Community School District Covers over 80 square miles and includes six different cities and townships in three different counties. A few years ago the South Lyon Community School District Unilaterally decided to reinstate the school resource officer following some Tragic events at other schools in the country. The school district then went Out to their member communities and asked them for contributions to fund that decision. Some Communities contributed, some did not. I believe that year three of the six communities contributed. The Stuhl district repeated that same process again last year and only two communities out of The six contributed. Each time the shortage was funded from the school district's general fund. I believe that the cost of the school resource officer is an operating expense for the school District, no different than providing food service, janitorial service, maintenance on their facilities, and security for their facilities. As such, I believe the Southland Community School District should accept that Responsibility and fund it directly, as it does with those other entities from the tax dollars it receives. Asking Them for additional funds from their budgets is again taxing them twice for That support. That additional cost is further exacerbated when some Communities do not contribute and even more money must be used from the school district's general fund to cover that shortage. Perhaps some of that savings could be used to fund the school resource officer. Again, I fully support the need for the school resource officer in keeping our students safe. However, I believe it is an operating expense for the South Lyon School District and they need to assume responsibility for Addressing it. [0:43:24](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I52bmSz49Bs&t=2604s) Thank you Councilmember Tonight I want to welcome Doug Bakke as our new city manager Doug's relationships with the city's residents For this, Doug's relationship with the city's residents, city employees, and the members of the City Council will help ensure ongoing growth and positive change for our city. So welcome, Doug. And speaking of change, there currently is some legislation pending in Lansing that I think folks need to be aware of. Because this legislation would restrict the abilities of local authorities to determine zoning requirements in their municipalities. The bills that have currently been introduced in the State House include House Bill 5529, Which prohibits local ordinances from requiring minimal parcel size or lot size for single Family residences where a subdivision is accessible. House Bill 5530 prohibits a minimum parcel size for detached single family residences Where a parcel is accessible and will be served by public water and sewer. House Bill 5531 limits the circumstances under which additional information can Be required for the same application after initial approval. So when council Says we need some more information that opportunity goes away. It creates a 60 -day decision shot clock after receipt of a site plan for a local unit of government. House Bill 5532 restricts the petition of how many people can Can actually contest a particular installation. I believe, as speaking as one of seven up here, That the local government you have directly elected Should oversee and manage the zoning requirements Within its boundaries, And determine what mix of structures best fits the needs and the vision of its residents, not Lansing. In addition, more bills are about to be introduced. The duplex by right, Which creates a statewide definition of duplex, And mandates that duplexes are a permitted use in any district where Single -family residences are are located so you can mix the duplexes and Single -family residences in the same area further the parking requirements Mandates that parking requirements are no more than one space per dwelling so When we have new apartment buildings and everything else you can have one space And I'm not sure where the other residents are going to park because it Takes away that opportunity to have that obligation

[0:45:52](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I52bmSz49Bs&t=2752s) It creates a statewide definition of Acceler accessory dwelling unit, mandates that ADUs Are permitted by right in residential zoning districts so that in different parcels you Could have two or more living structures, okay, without having to worry about meeting Impervious surface requirements, plot coverage, et cetera. It allows mobile homes in any residential zone. Zone. Setback requirements, it mandates setback requirements of 15 feet or less from the front Property line. Most of our setbacks are what, 35 feet or more? Thirty -five. Okay. Side to side, could be five feet or less. That close. Okay. If the local government is located within a metropolitan area or located adjacent to A specific area. Dwelling size, it prohibits a minimum area requirement for the dwelling. The minute the state takes control of local zoning ordinances, they can pretty well dictate What you are required to put in the city, be it data centers or housing units, and how Tightly packed those structures can be placed next to each other. Zoning control should be restricted to the local level, not administered and controlled By the state. Again, my opinion, one of seven. The residents of the city know what is best for their town, how they want it to look, And how they want to live. So if you agree, I'm asking you to contact your state representative and tell him to oppose these bills. Our state representative is Jason Morgan, and he can be contacted at jasonmorgan at house .mi .gov Or by calling him at 517 -373 -0855. As SEMCOG has so eloquently summarized this issue, Issue, sweeping mandates oversimplify the problem and ignore the unique needs and circumstances of Michigan's diverse communities. SEMCOG can also provide additional information if you will contact Nikki Hartley, SEMCOG's Government Affairs Specialist, at 313 -949 -7445. So please, I ask you to get involved, let your representative know how you feel about These bills that the state wants to push through and remove control from the Local government and with that I'll look for a motion to adjourn and a second Councilmember Kurtzweil moved to adjourn second see you in two weeks thanks so Very much
